tasks.title: Thread optional handlers['expected_fs_signature'] through run_pipeline into DetonationChamber.detonate
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/pipeline.py is replaced byte-for-byte with the validated whole-file content from the brief.

run_pipeline reads an OPTIONAL expected_fs_signature via handlers.get('expected_fs_signature') and passes it as the keyword-only argument expected_fs_signature=... to every chamber.detonate(...) call.
When handlers has no 'expected_fs_signature' key the value is None and behavior is identical to today (chamber's no-signature path applies).
When a string expected_fs_signature is supplied with a 5-tuple runner result, the verdict reaches 'confirmed' via the chamber's semantic_verdict gate.
run_pipeline signature stays (handlers, *, success_marker='VULNERABLE') -> dict; expected_fs_signature is never positional/required.
The hunt->triage->poc->detonate->report->done state-machine transition sequence and the returned {'phase','reports','report'} dict shape are unchanged.
Module stays pure and deterministic (stdlib + ngv2 only): no fork/execve/subprocess/network/clock/random work, no module-level state, no I/O.
verification_command passes green (the four committed tests/test_pipeline.py flow tests).
No test files are authored or modified; the committed oracle tests/test_pipeline.py is authoritative.

spec.objective: Edit the existing short module ngv2/pipeline.py so that run_pipeline threads an OPTIONAL expected_fs_signature read from the injected handlers dict into every DetonationChamber.detonate call as the keyword-only argument expected_fs_signature=..., so that a genuine filesystem-effect PoC reaches the strong semantic gate inside the chamber and resolves to 'confirmed', while behavior is otherwise identical to today when the key is absent.
functional_requirements: Inside run_pipeline, read expected_fs_signature = handlers.get('expected_fs_signature') (returns None when the key is absent) and pass it as the keyword-only argument expected_fs_signature=... to every chamber.detonate(poc, handlers.get('target_spec'), handlers['runner'], ...) call.

Preserve run_pipeline's signature (handlers, *, success_marker='VULNERABLE') -> dict, the hunt->triage->poc->detonate->report->done HuntStateMachine transition sequence, the existing handler-key contract (hunt/triage/poc/runner/target_spec/report), and the returned {'phase','reports','report'} dict shape.

Keep the module pure and deterministic — stdlib + ngv2 imports only (DetonationChamber, HuntStateMachine), no module-level state, no I/O, no logging, no randomness, and no real fork/execve/subprocess/network/clock work; expected_fs_signature must never be positional or required.
spec.interfaces: run_pipeline(handlers: dict, *, success_marker: str='VULNERABLE') -> dict. Consumes the read-only ngv2.detonation.DetonationChamber.detonate(self, poc, target_spec, runner, *, expected_fs_signature=None) -> LiveTestReport (string signature routes through semantic_verdict over an fs_snapshot_diff drawn from a 4-tuple/5-tuple runner result) and read-only ngv2.state_machine.HuntStateMachine. New optional handlers key: 'expected_fs_signature' (str or absent).
edge_cases: handlers['expected_fs_signature'] set to a string with a 5-tuple runner result -> fs-effect PoC reaches 'confirmed' (mirrors oracle test_run_pipeline_full_flow_confirmed).
'expected_fs_signature' key absent -> handlers.get(...) is None and the marker-only no-signature chamber path applies -> 'inconclusive' (mirrors oracle test_run_pipeline_marker_only_is_inconclusive).
Triage drops findings and the no-findings flow still walk to phase 'done' with the unchanged dict shape.
An optional 'report' handler is invoked with (state, reports); absent 'report' key yields report=None.
non_goals: Do NOT add integration/e2e tests and do NOT author or modify any test — the committed oracle tests/test_pipeline.py is authoritative.
Do NOT modify ngv2/detonation.py, ngv2/poc_runner.py, ngv2/poc_runner_live.py, ngv2/handlers.py, ngv2/contracts.py, ngv2/state_machine.py, or any module other than ngv2/pipeline.py.
Do NOT change run_pipeline's signature, the handler-key contract, the state-machine transition sequence, or the returned dict shape.
Do NOT make expected_fs_signature positional/required, and do NOT invent a different handler contract (e.g. a handlers['pocs'] list).
Do NOT perform any real fork/execve/subprocess/network/clock/random work.
spec.implementation_notes:
Whole-file replacement of a SHORT module. Ship ngv2/pipeline.py EXACTLY as the validated content embedded in the brief, byte-for-byte. The only behavioral delta vs the current file is the two added lines inside run_pipeline: `expected_fs_signature = handlers.get('expected_fs_signature')` before building reports, and passing `expected_fs_signature=expected_fs_signature` as the keyword-only argument in the chamber.detonate(...) comprehension. Keep the module/function docstrings, the two `from ngv2.* import` lines, and the `from __future__ import annotations` as in the brief.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: No new test data and no authored tests. The committed, authoritative oracle tests/test_pipeline.py supplies injected handler callables (hunt/triage/poc/runner), a string handlers['expected_fs_signature'] with a 5-tuple runner result for the confirmed case, the absent-key marker-only inconclusive case, and the triage-drop / report-handler / no-findings flow fixtures. Integration tests are EXCUSED via Non-Goals.

token_budget_ratio.note: Tiny two-line whole-file edit; no tests are authored, so the test-token budget is reserved solely for running and confirming the committed oracle tests/test_pipeline.py flow tests (verification_command), which dominate validation effort relative to the trivial edit.
